So after one action, the player moves from (38,10) to (36,10). The level says "1 actions taken on this level". So they have taken one action already? Or they have taken 1 action? The description: "ARC-AGI-3 game, level 1, 1 actions taken on this level, 64x64 grid." Means they have taken 1 action (maybe they already moved?). The learned action effects: action 1: moves dark-blue 2x2 by (dy=-2, dx=0). So the only known action moves the player up by 2.

Thus the player can only move up in steps of 2? Possibly repeated actions? But only one action known. The goal likely is to move the player onto/against some object. Since the only movement is up, we need to see which objects are vertically aligned above the player at positions reachable by moving up multiples of 2.

Player initial at (38,10). Moving up by -2 reduces y coordinate (assuming y is row index increasing downwards). So new y = 36, then 34, 32, 30, 28, etc. x stays 10.

Thus the player can only occupy columns x=10, y decreasing by multiples of 2.

Now look at objects coordinates:

- 11× black 2x2 at (10,32), (14,32), (18,32), … So there is a black 2x2 at (10,32). That's exactly x=1
